flexible.text: Adopt the `crossplane/upjet-provider-template@main` layout: `apis/cluster`, `apis/namespaced`, `internal/controller/cluster`, `internal/controller/namespaced`, `GetProvider()` and `GetProviderNamespaced()`, and `pipeline.Run(pc, pns, root)`.

Pin `github.com/vmware/terraform-provider-vsphere` at pseudo-version `v1.26.1-0.20260319130334-b2eabd5702e1`, which is tag v2.15.1 at commit b2eabd57, with a go.mod comment explaining why the version string looks unusual.
Target `github.com/crossplane/upjet/v2` v2.5.0 and set the go directive to `1.26.8` so it matches upjet's floor.

Implement references with `config.Reference{TerraformName: ...}` in the shared VM configurator: datacenter_id to vsphere_datacenter; resource_pool_id to vsphere_resource_pool; datastore_id to vsphere_vmfs_datastore (NAS datastores via a literal datastoreId); datastore_cluster_id to vsphere_datastore_cluster; host_system_id to vsphere_host; folder to vsphere_folder using its path; network_interface.network_id to vsphere_distributed_port_group; storage_policy_id to vsphere_vm_storage_policy. Fix the VirtualDisk datacenter and datastore references with correct extractors.

Configure LateInitializer IgnoredFields and, where needed, custom diff suppression for provider-defaulted VM fields: `ept_rvi_mode`, `hv_mode`, plus any field the lab e2e shows round-tripping. Set VM operation timeouts long enough for clone and OVF deploy.

Implement the session cache in `internal/clients`, keyed by ProviderConfig kind, namespace and name plus a SHA-256 of the extracted credentials. Store the configured `vsphere.Provider()` Meta, evict on authentication or session errors, and protect it with a mutex.

Parse credentials into typed values: booleans accept true, false and their string forms; api_timeout accepts a number or a numeric string. Return errors that name the offending key, and never log secret values.

Add the upjet v2 scraper go:generate step reading the pulled `docs/resources` from the vmware repo so `config/provider-metadata.yaml` is real, and hand-write `examples/cluster/virtualmachine/`, `examples/namespaced/virtualmachine/`, and ProviderConfig, ClusterProviderConfig and Secret examples.
RELEASING.md documents the interactive docker login, `make build.all publish`, verifying the index, creating `latest` with `docker buildx imagetools create`, and the `vX.Y.Z-N` fix-tag rule.
Declare the SafeStart capability in `package/crossplane.yaml` and wire the template's gated setup in `cmd/provider/main.go`; the lab e2e records whether it engaged but does not gate on it.

Add a manually-run lab e2e target that installs Crossplane (parameterized version) and the provider tag on the current kube context. It reads lab IDs and credentials from environment variables, applies cluster and namespaced VM examples, asserts the US-002, US-005 and US-006 criteria, and cleans up.
Add Go unit tests for credential parsing and session-cache keying and eviction, run in CI and not a release gate.
Commit order: toolchain and build submodule; upjet v2 skeleton and hand-written code; shared configurators; generated code in its own commits; packaging and image; docs, CI and cleanup.
With 100 VMs on one ProviderConfig, the provider holds one vCenter session per pod for that ProviderConfig in steady state.
The runtime image contains only the provider binary on a current alpine base, with no Terraform and no network fetch at startup, so it works in Pioneer airgap mode.
No credential of any kind (Docker Hub or vCenter) is committed; e2e and release read credentials only from the environment or an interactive login.
`make generate` is deterministic: a second run yields zero diff.

acceptance_criteria.text: "Build/generate/lint clean"
Setting `TERRAFORM_VERSION=1.6.0` makes `make generate` fail with the check-terraform-version error before any download (error case).
The built runtime image contains no `terraform` binary and no provider plugin zip; `docker run --entrypoint sh` shows no `/usr/local/bin/terraform` and no `/terraform/provider-mirror` (edge case).
Running `make generate` twice in a row produces no git diff.

On k3s with Crossplane v2.2.0 and again with v2.4.2, a cluster-scoped `virtualmachine.vsphere.alphabravo.io/v1alpha1` VirtualMachine and a namespaced `virtualmachine.vsphere.m.alphabravo.io/v1alpha1` VirtualMachine using Pioneer's field profile both reach Ready=True and Synced=True.
Changing `numCpus` or `memory` on each VM updates it in place without recreate, and deleting each MR removes the VM from vCenter.
A namespaced VM whose providerConfigRef names a missing ProviderConfig reports Synced=False with a message naming the missing config (error case).
Installing the package on a Crossplane older than v2.0.0 is rejected by the package manager (edge case).
"Published v2.15.1"
`crane manifest docker.io/alphabravodevops/provider-vsphere:v2.15.1` returns an OCI image index with linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 entries, and the lab e2e installs the provider from that exact tag.
Running the publish target without a prior `docker login` fails without pushing anything, and no credential file is added to git (error case).
All pre-existing `2.12.0-terraform-vsphere*` tags still resolve after the release, and `latest` resolves to the v2.15.1 index digest only after the e2e passed (edge case).
"Fix + add core VM refs (Recommended)"
A VirtualMachine using `resourcePoolIdRef` to a ResourcePool MR resolves `resourcePoolId` to that pool's ID, not a compute cluster ID.
A reference to an MR that is not yet Ready leaves the VM unresolved with a ReferencesResolved-style condition instead of an empty ID (error case).
`datastoreIdRef` resolves when it points at a VmfsDatastore; a NasDatastore is used by setting a literal `datastoreId`, because an upjet reference field targets one kind (edge case).
"Proactive + test (Recommended)"
After a VM is Ready, 3 consecutive poll cycles show no update calls for provider-defaulted fields such as `eptRviMode` and `hvMode`.

A VM powered off out of band stays powered off after the next reconcile when an unrelated field such as `annotation` is changed out of band; a change made in the MR spec may power the VM on, as vSphere provider 2.15.1 does after any reconfigure (error case).
"Cache per ProviderConfig (Recommended)"
During the lab e2e, the vCenter session count attributed to the provider user stays at or below the number of distinct ProviderConfigs per provider pod across at least 3 poll intervals.
Rotating the password in the credentials Secret makes the next reconcile use a new client and succeed; the old cached client is not reused (error case).
"MIGRATION.md in repo (Recommended)"

MIGRATION.md contains one row per inventory resource with legacy group/kind and new cluster and namespaced group/kind, and names the Pioneer files `internal/operator/manifest/machines_network.go`, `internal/operator/manifest/resources_vmware.go`, `internal/operator/statussync/watcher.go`, `internal/operator/lifecycle/seed_ip_resolver.go`, `internal/operator/manifest/crossplane.go`, `internal/airgap/bom/registry.go`.
MIGRATION.md warns that a namespaced MR without providerConfigRef defaults to a ClusterProviderConfig named default (edge case).
"Minimal PR CI (Recommended)"
A PR triggers one workflow running golangci-lint v2, generate plus check-diff, build for both arches, unit tests and crddiff, with no registry login step.
`hack/prepare.sh`, `examples/storeconfig/vault.yaml` and the Upbound backport, commands, e2e and tag workflows no longer exist (edge case).

observable_truths.text: `make generate`, `make lint` and `make build.all` succeed on a clean checkout, and a second `make generate` leaves `git status` clean.
`make generate` with TERRAFORM_VERSION=1.6.0 fails at the version guard.
The runtime image filesystem contains no terraform binary and no provider mirror directory.
`go.mod` requires `github.com/crossplane/upjet/v2 v2.5.0` and the vsphere pseudo-version for tag v2.15.1; no `github.com/upbound/upjet` import remains.
Every generated controller uses the TerraformPluginSDK async connector; `grep -r NewWorkspaceStore internal/` returns nothing.
`package/crds` contains exactly 45 CRDs in `*.vsphere.alphabravo.io` groups and 45 in `*.vsphere.m.alphabravo.io` groups, plus the provider-config CRDs.
No generated Kind starts with `VSphere`.
Every generated MR CRD serves only version v1alpha1.
`vsphere_distributed_virtual_switch_pvlan_mapping` and `vsphere_configuration_profile` exist as DistributedVirtualSwitchPvlanMapping and ConfigurationProfile in both scopes.
No CRD description contains the text `<no value>`, and `examples-generated/` exists after `make generate`.
The VM CRD in both scopes exposes Ref and Selector fields for datacenterId, resourcePoolId, datastoreId, datastoreClusterId, hostSystemId, folder, networkInterface networkId and storagePolicyId.
A Secret with allow_unverified_ssl as the string true and one with the boolean true both configure the provider successfully.
A Secret missing vsphere_server yields a Synced=False condition message containing vsphere_server.
Two MRs sharing one ProviderConfig cause exactly one vsphere Provider Configure call per pod until the credentials change.
After a vCenter authentication error the cache entry is evicted and the next reconcile configures a new client.
The provider starts with SafeStart gating when CRD watch RBAC is present and falls back to eager setup otherwise, logging which path it took.
Cluster and namespaced VirtualMachine MRs with Pioneer's field profile reach Ready and Synced on Crossplane v2.2.0 and v2.4.2.
A Ready VM shows no repeated update operations for three poll intervals.

An out-of-band powered-off VM is not powered on by an out-of-band change to a field Crossplane does not manage (an optional, provider-computed, late-init-ignored field not set in forProvider, such as annotation); drift on other fields, including unset fields enforced as their schema default or zero value, is corrected and may power the VM on, which is documented.
resourcePoolIdRef to a ResourcePool resolves to the pool ID.
Deleting each VM MR removes the VM from vCenter.
docker.io/alphabravodevops/provider-vsphere:v2.15.1 is an OCI index with linux/amd64 and linux/arm64.
Legacy 2.12.0 tags still resolve after release, and latest equals the v2.15.1 digest.
package/crossplane.yaml declares a Crossplane constraint of v2.0.0 or newer.
No file in the repository contains Docker Hub or vCenter credentials.
RELEASING.md states the v2.15.1-N rule for provider-only fixes.
The only workflow file is ci.yml, and it has no registry login step.
hack/prepare.sh, examples/storeconfig and cluster/test/setup.sh are absent.
MIGRATION.md lists all 45 resources with legacy and new group and kind.
README.md documents install by fully qualified multi-arch tag, the credentials Secret keys, and a VM example.
`go test ./internal/clients/...` runs the credential and cache unit tests.

destination_naming_rule: Each Terraform resource `vsphere_X` keeps its current short group and is generated twice: `SHORTGROUP.vsphere.alphabravo.io` (cluster-scoped) and `SHORTGROUP.vsphere.m.alphabravo.io` (namespaced), both at version v1alpha1. Kind = legacy Kind with only the leading `VSphere` prefix stripped, remaining casing unchanged. New resources: `vsphere_distributed_virtual_switch_pvlan_mapping` becomes networking/DistributedVirtualSwitchPvlanMapping; `vsphere_configuration_profile` becomes hostandclustermanagement/ConfigurationProfile. Provider config types live in `vsphere.alphabravo.io` (cluster) and `vsphere.m.alphabravo.io` (namespaced).
